newsitem.title: USA: Home mortgage rates fall in week.
newsitem.headline: Home mortgage rates fall in week.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week as news that inflation was under control eased fears of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 8.14 percent in the week ended Sept. 20, down from 8.28 percent last week. Fifteen-year mortgages fell to 7.64 percent from 7.81 percent. One-year adjustable mortgage rates dipped to an average of 5.83 percent from 5.90 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.57 percent, the 15-year 7.09 percent and the adjustable mortgage 5.77 percent.

"A favourable CPI (Consumer Price Index) report earlier in the week helped lower interest rates by allaying fears of inflation," Freddie Mac Chief Economist Robert Van Order said. On Friday, the Labour Department said August consumer prices rose a mere 0.1 percent.
Van Order said, however, that Thursday's strong housing starts report will cause interest rates and mortgage rates to rise next week.
The Commerce Department said Thursday that August housing starts rose 4.5 percent to a 1.525 million unit annual rate, the highest level since March 1994.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Sept. 24, and many economists expect the Fed to raise interest rates then.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the adjustable mortgage, also unchanged from the previous week.
